output.title: Naming conventions are a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
output.body:
If you run a small business, naming conventions are not cosmetic. They are a design constraint on whether one recurring workflow can move cleanly between your CRM, inbox, invoicing tool, and spreadsheets without someone translating fields by hand.

That matters before you automate. If a customer ID, invoice number, or lead status changes format from one system to the next, the problem is not just tidy filing. It is translation work. And translation work gets paid for somewhere, either in manual effort or in maintenance.

The choice is simple: standardise the naming up front, or automate around the legacy names and keep paying the translation cost in rules, prompts, and exceptions. If money is involved, keep the boundary clear: human approval stays mandatory for any payment or other high-risk decision.

A practical next step is to pick one recurring workflow this week — customer enquiries, lead tracking, or invoice processing — and map the field names from source to destination. Write down every place you rename, reformat, or guess. That map is your naming blueprint. Once you have it, you can see whether the naming layer is the real constraint, or whether the rest of the workflow is. Labels do not improve by wishful thinking.
